claims.text: Sec. 9007(a) establishes the Review Board 'as an independent agency' with nine members appointed by the President by and with the advice and consent of the Senate.

Sec. 9007(b)(4)(A) bars anyone with 'any previous or current involvement with any legacy program or controlling authority relating to the collection, exploitation, or reverse engineering of technologies of unknown origin.'
Sec. 9009(c)(1) requires disclosure absent 'clear and convincing evidence' for postponement, inverting the default classification presumption.
In enacted law the equivalent judgement is made not by an independent board but by 'the original classification authority' under Sec. 1843(a) of P.L. 118-31.

desc: The Review Board is the JFK Records Act transplant at the centre of the UAPDA and the thing the conference was most determined to prevent. Section 9007 establishes it 'as an independent agency' — outside the Department of Defense, outside the intelligence community, outside the armed services and intelligence committees. The President appoints nine citizens 'by and with the advice and consent of the Senate,' with nominations due within 90 days of enactment and a replacement nomination required within 30 days of any Senate rejection. Nominees are drawn from recommendations by the four congressional leaders, the Secretary of Defense, the National Academy of Sciences, 'established nonprofit research organizations relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena,' and the American Historical Association. The disqualification in Section 9007(b)(4)(A) is the operative clause: members 'shall be impartial citizens, none of whom shall have had any previous or current involvement with any legacy program or controlling authority relating to the collection, exploitation, or reverse engineering of technologies of unknown origin or the examination of biological evidence of living or deceased non-human intelligence.' The composition is mandated to include a national security official, a foreign service official, a scientist or engineer, an economist, a professional historian and a sociologist. Under Section 9009(c)(1) the Board must order disclosure 'in the absence of clear and convincing evidence' for postponement — reversing the ordinary classification presumption. Under Section 9010(b) recovered material must be made available to it for personal examination. The Board was removed in conference and does not exist. Nothing in enacted law performs its function: under Section 1843 of P.L. 118-31 the postponement decision is made by 'the original classification authority.'
